acs.text_first_line: AC1 The service and the three operations are deployed with the rwb-integration login
AC2 The worker registers the sweep workflow and its three activities
AC3 The next-action-check Schedule is created and reported
AC4 The flag governs the sweep and the operations
AC5 The backfill fills only the missing cases and is idempotent
AC6 The five dashboard series, the three alerts and the runbook cover the sweep

gap_rows.title: rwb-integration next action deployment: the login and secret reference, the next-action-check run values, the alert thresholds and the runbook ownership are not fixed by a source
gap_rows.source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42 and 44; Ownership Map tables job_catalog (P2) and feature_flag (PLT) and API row GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action (owner P3); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 12, 13, 27 and 28; TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (job_catalog, feature_flag), API-P2-009 and Appendix T-B; legacy RWB-E2-035 §4 step 7, §12 job step and §13 configuration; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R5.7, §R7.2 s12 and §R9
gap_rows.section: §3 Preconditions, §10 Authority, §11 Data, §12.5 to §12.7, §13 Solution plan
gap_rows.description: One combined row for the deployment side of this key. (1) Login and identity: no source names the login, the secret reference or the worker identity of rwb-integration under DP-02, and the release must carry one login and one task queue. (2) Ownership conflict: the Ownership Map keeps GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action with P3 while this work package assigns it to rwb-integration, so the release deploys a path the map attributes to another service until the ruling is entered. (3) Contract field names: the release configures the consumed shapes of the P3 case read and write, the catalog operation of RWB-P3-E2042-CON, the P3 reference data and parameter reads and the P7 decision log read, whose JSON property names and query parameters are fixed by no source; the readiness probe must therefore name a check that does not depend on an invented field. (4) Operation names: the release exposes POST /next-actions:resolve, GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action and POST /cases/{caseId}/next-action, and the colon path and the fill method are this work package's. (5) Schedule: the release creates next-action-check every 5 minutes with the overlap policy SKIP, and the catch-up window, the overlap window and the backfill limit are not specified, while Arch v5 slide 44 lists JOB-05 as retired durable timers and the timer table ruling retires it, so the job_catalog row is the only legacy trace of the sweep. (6) Message texts: the three alerts carry MSG-P2-023, MSG-P3-027 and MSG-GEN-004, whose texts come from the legacy story and the platform catalogue and not from a deployment source. (7) Rule values: the series and the alerts name package version RES-2026.12 and the rows R-RES-04 and R-SET-13, which are legacy values kept unchanged and must match the registry rows of RWB-E2-042. (8) Timer vocabulary: the runbook and the alert texts name the sweep by its new name, and the legacy JOB-05 wording survives in the criteria and in the job catalogue, so the two are mapped in the runbook.
gap_rows.evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-035 §13 fixes no deployment value and names no identity; TSD P2 Integration v3 API-P2-009 reads the job catalogue with owner, schedule, run book and alert threshold but names no next action job; Arch v5 slide 44 lists JOB-05 as every 5 min, owner all, retired durable timers; the Ownership Map gives job_catalog to P2 and feature_flag to PLT; no source fixes the readiness check, the catch-up window, the backfill limit or the alert thresholds of this sweep.
gap_rows.owner_role: DevOps engineer; platform administrator; platform workflow kit owner
gap_rows.proposed: Fix the identity, the secret reference and the probe checks in RWB-P2-E2035-OPS; take the catch-up window, the overlap window, the backfill limit and the thresholds as values of the environment; create the next-action-check row in the job catalogue with its run book path; record the read path ruling in the Ownership Map; and review the three runbook entries with the on-call rota.

asm_rows.text: The release carries the rwb-integration login as a secret reference from the platform secret store and runs the worker as that identity on the task queue rwb-integration; the readiness probe waits for one successful poll and one successful authorise call, and neither probe writes to the database.
asm_rows.why: No source names the worker identity, the secret reference or the probe checks of this service, and DP-02 and DP-10 require one login and one task queue per service.
asm_rows.read: Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-02 and DP-10; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27 (worker versioning and build ID); ASM-1177.
asm_rows.confirm: ACE team, DBA and platform administrator
asm_rows.impact: The chart and the probes are fixed in the values of the environment; a wrong identity fails the registration check and never reaches production.

asm_rows.text: The three alerts use thresholds and routes that are values of the environment: the missing-action backlog alert routes to the team manager of the team and the platform on-call, the NoPackageInForce alert routes to RW-COE, and the sweep-stalled alert fires when no run completes inside twice the cadence or when a consumed-call failure rate passes its threshold; each alert carries one message ID and one runbook entry.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story sets no alert and no threshold, and Architecture v5 slide 44 and ADR-023 fix the mechanism but not the values.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 44; ADR-023 (observability per service); Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s12 and s14; legacy RWB-E2-035 §14 (MSG-P2-023, MSG-P3-027, MSG-GEN-004).
asm_rows.applied_in: §7 AC6, §11 Data, §13 Alert mapping and §14 of RWB-P2-E2035-OPS
asm_rows.confirm: DevOps engineer, platform on-call rota and RW-COE
asm_rows.impact: A threshold change is a values change and not a code change; the three messages stay the ones the case record and the catalogue already carry.

asm_rows.text: The smoke run and the backfill tests use the synthetic cases RW-2026-000401, RW-2026-000402 and RW-2026-000403 of the legacy criteria in DEV and SIT only, seeded by the pipeline of the owning stories, and no production case is read or filled by the deployment.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story gives the case identifiers of its criteria and no source names a fixture owner, a seeding path or an evidence format for a deployment test.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-035 §7 (case identifiers of AC1 to AC14); RWB-ITG-E2035-ITG §3 and §4 (the seeded cases); Template and Rules v1 §R9.
asm_rows.impact: The smoke run and the backfill test are repeatable and synthetic; a fixture change is a pipeline change and not a story change.
